```{r}
#| label: setup

library(tidyverse)

# palette from the slide theme

pal_sex <- c(Male = fact, Female = counter)

theme_set(
  theme_minimal(base_size = 15) +
    theme(panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
          legend.position = "bottom",
```

## The data

`nlme::Orthodont`: distance (mm) from the pituitary to the pterygomaxillary fissure in **27 children** (16 boys, 11 girls) at ages **8, 10, 12, 14** [@PotthoffRoy64].

::: {style="font-size: 0.9em"}

```{r}
#| label: data
ortho <- as_tibble(nlme::Orthodont) |>
  mutate(Subject = factor(as.character(Subject)),  # unordered id
         age_c = age - 8)                          # 0 = first visit
ortho
```

:::

::: {.note}
As with `Chick`, `Subject` comes as an **ordered** factor: convert it. `Sex` has levels `Male`, `Female`: **boys are the reference**.
:::

# {.divider background-color="#f7f6f3"}

<p class="eyebrow">Part A · Look first</p>
<p class="bignum">A</p>
<h2>Questions 1–3</h2>
<p class="lead muted">Design, individual curves, mean profiles.</p>

---

## 1. How many children, how many measurements?

::: {.columns}

::: {.column width="60%"}

::: {style="font-size: 0.8em"}

```{r}
#| label: q1-count
ortho |>
  summarise(children = n_distinct(Subject),
            measurements = n(), .by = Sex)
```

```{r}
#| label: q1-visits
ortho |>
  count(Subject, name = "visits") |>
  count(visits, name = "children")
```

:::
:::

::: {.column width="40%"}

::: {.incremental}
- **27 children**, **108 measurements**: every child has the **4 visits**.
- **Balanced** (same ages for everybody), **complete** (no drop-out), **equally spaced**.
- Opposite to `ChickWeight` (unbalanced, drop-out, 12 times).
:::



:::

:::

---

## 2. Spaghetti plot: the random part

::: {.columns}

::: {.column width="55%"}

::: {style="font-size: 0.53em"}

```{r}
#| fig-height: 5.2
#| fig-width: 7
ggplot(ortho, aes(age, distance, group = Subject, color = Sex)) +
  geom_line(alpha = .6) +
  geom_point(alpha = .6, size = 1.2) +
  stat_summary(aes(group = 1), fun = mean, geom = "line", color = "#1d2b30", linewidth = 1.6) +
  stat_summary(aes(group = 1), fun = mean, geom = "point", color = "#1d2b30", size = 2.5) +
  facet_wrap(~ Sex) +
  scale_color_manual(values = c(Male = "#2a9d8f", Female = "#e76f51"), guide = "none") +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = c(8, 10, 12, 14)) +
  labs(x = "age (years)", y = "distance (mm)")
```

:::

:::

::: {.column width="45%"}

::: {style="font-size: 0.62em"}

**What we see → what it implies**

::: {.incremental}
- Each child **stays high or low** across visits (rarely cross) → measurements of a child are **correlated (not independent)**: a mixed model, not `lm()`.
- Children **start at very different intercepts** (≈ 17–28 mm at age 8), even within a sex → maybe each child its own level (random intercept): `(1 | Subject)`.
- Within a sex, lines are **roughly parallel** → maybe each child does not need its own rate (no random slope). The spread **does not fan out** with age → if children differ in rate, not by much.
:::


:::

::: {.fragment .keybox}
The spaghetti plot is about **each child vs its group mean** (black line): it decides **ONLY the random part**.
:::

:::

:::


---

## 3. Mean profiles: the fixed part

::: {.columns}

::: {.column width="55%"}

::: {style="font-size: 0.55em"}


```{r}
#| label: q3-means
#| fig-height: 5.2
#| fig-width: 7
prof <- ortho |>
  summarise(m = mean(distance), se = sd(distance) / sqrt(n()),
            .by = c(Sex, age))

ggplot(prof, aes(age, m, color = Sex)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 1) +
  geom_pointrange(aes(ymin = m - 2 * se, ymax = m + 2 * se),
                  position = position_dodge(.3), size = .4) +
  scale_color_manual(values = c(Male = "#2a9d8f", Female = "#e76f51")) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = c(8, 10, 12, 14)) +
  labs(x = "age (years)", y = "mean distance (mm) ± 2 SE")
```

:::

:::

::: {.column width="45%"}

::: {style="font-size: 0.55em"}

```{r}
#| label: q3-gap
prof |>
  select(Sex, age, m) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = Sex, values_from = m) |>
  mutate(gap = Male - Female)
```

:::

::: {style="font-size: 0.62em"}

**What we see → what it implies**

::: {.incremental}
- Means rise in a **straight line** and **changes by age** → `age_c` as fixed effect (linear, no `I(age_c^2)`).
- Boys **above** girls at every age → `Sex` as fixed effect
- The gap **widens** (`r round(diff(rev(prof$m[prof$age == 8])), 1)` → `r round(diff(rev(prof$m[prof$age == 14])), 1)` mm): lines **not parallel** → a different **mean** rate for boys and girls: may exists interaction `age_c:Sex` (the rate depends on sex)
:::

:::

:::

:::

# {.divider background-color="#f7f6f3"}

<p class="eyebrow">Part B · Model</p>
<p class="bignum">B</p>
<h2>Questions 4–5</h2>
<p class="lead muted">Random intercept or intercept + slope? And why centre age?</p>


---

## 4. Random intercept vs intercept + slope

::: {style="font-size: 0.75em"}

```{r}
o1 <- lmer(distance ~ age_c * Sex + (1 | Subject), data = ortho) # random intercept
o1_add <- lmer(distance ~ age_c + Sex + (1 | Subject), data = ortho) 
o2 <- lmer(distance ~ age_c * Sex + (1 + age_c | Subject), data = ortho) # random intercept
o2_add <- lmer(distance ~ age_c + Sex + (1 + age_c | Subject), data = ortho) # random intercept
```

:::

random part: **is the random slope needed?**

```{r}
anova(o1, o2) # random part: is the random slope needed?
```

Answer: **no, including random slope does not improve enough**

---

## 4. Random intercept vs intercept + slope

::: {style="font-size: 0.75em"}


```{r}
#| label: q4-fit
o1 <- lmer(distance ~ age_c * Sex + (1 | Subject), data = ortho) # random intercept
o1_add <- lmer(distance ~ age_c + Sex + (1 | Subject), data = ortho) 
o2 <- lmer(distance ~ age_c * Sex + (1 + age_c | Subject), data = ortho) # random intercept
o2_add <- lmer(distance ~ age_c + Sex + (1 + age_c | Subject), data = ortho) # random intercept
```

:::

**Is the interaction needed?**

```{r}
anova(o1_add, o1) # fixed part: is age_c:Sex needed?
```

Answer: Yes

* `age_c + Sex`: **parallel lines**: same growth rate, constant boy–girl gap.
* `age_c * Sex` = `age_c + Sex + age_c:Sex`: **each sex its own slope** (`age_c:SexFemale` is the difference in growth rate, so the gap changes with age)


::: {.keybox}
It agrees with the plot: different starts, roughly parallel lines within each sex, but different growth rates for each sex.
:::

---

## 4. Final model

::: {style="font-size: 0.55em"}


```{r}
o1 <- lmer(distance ~ age_c * Sex + (1 | Subject), data = ortho)
o1
```

:::

::: {style="font-size: 0.67em"}


$$
\texttt{distance} \sim \texttt{age_c * Sex} + \texttt{(1  | Subject)}
$$

| Term | What it says | Seen in | Parameter |
|---|---|---|---|
| `(Intercept)` | mean distance of **boys at age 8** (reference) | mean profiles: where the boys' line starts | $\beta_0$ |
| `age_c` | distance grows **linearly** with age | mean profiles: straight lines | $\beta_1$ |
| `SexFemale` | boys and girls differ **at age 8** (female - reference) | mean profiles: boys above | $\beta_2$ |
| `age_c:SexFemale  ` | boys and girls grow at a different **mean rate** | mean profiles: gap widens | $\beta_3$ |


:::


---

## 5. Why `age_c = age - 8`?

::: {.lead}
Same model, two ways of measuring age. Only the **meaning** of `(Intercept)` and `SexFemale` changes.
:::

::: {style="font-size: 0.75em"}

| | with `age` | with `age_c = age - 8` |
|---|---|---|
| "time 0" is | **age 0** (a newborn) | **age 8** (first visit) |
| `(Intercept)` = boys at time 0 | `r round(fixef(o1)[1] - 8 * fixef(o1)[2], 2)` mm | `r round(fixef(o1)[1], 2)` mm |
| `SexFemale` = girl − boy at time 0 | `r round(fixef(o1)[3] - 8 * fixef(o1)[4], 2)` mm | `r round(fixef(o1)[3], 2)` mm |
| `age`/`age_c`, `…:SexFemale` (slopes) | `r round(fixef(o1)[2], 3)`, `r round(fixef(o1)[4], 3)` | `r round(fixef(o1)[2], 3)`, `r round(fixef(o1)[4], 3)` |

:::

::: {.keybox}
With `age`, the model says girls are **`r round(fixef(o1)[3] - 8 * fixef(o1)[4], 1)` mm bigger at birth**: an extrapolation 8 years outside the data, with the **opposite sign** to what we see. With `age_c`, both numbers describe the first visit, where we have data.
:::

::: {.note}
Values with `age` obtained from `o1` by moving the origin: intercept − 8 · slope. Fitting `age * Sex` gives exactly the same numbers.
:::

# {.divider background-color="#f7f6f3"}

<p class="eyebrow">Part C · Read the model</p>
<p class="bignum">C</p>
<h2>Questions 6–7</h2>
<p class="lead muted">From `o1`, by hand.</p>

---

## 6. By hand from `fixef(o1)`

::: {style="font-size: 0.7em"}

```{r}
#| label: q6-fixef
fixef(o1)
```

```{r}
#| echo: false
b <- fixef(o1)
```

:::

::: {.note}
Boys are the reference: their values are `(Intercept)` and `age_c` alone; girls add `SexFemale` and `age_c:SexFemale`.
:::


::: {style="font-size: 0.65em"}

| | **Age 8** (`age_c` = 0) | **Age 14** (`age_c` = 6) | **mm/year** |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Boys** | $\beta_0$ = `r round(b[1], 3)` | $\beta_0 + 6\beta_1$ = `r round(b[1] + 6 * b[2], 3)` | $\beta_1$ = `r round(b[2], 3)` |
| **Girls** | $\beta_0 + \beta_2$ = `r round(b[1] + b[3], 3)` | $\beta_0 + \beta_2 + 6(\beta_1 + \beta_3)$ = `r round(b[1] + b[3] + 6 * (b[2] + b[4]), 2)` | $\beta_1 + \beta_3$ = `r round(b[2] + b[4], 3)` |
| **Gap** (boy − girl) | $-\beta_2$ = `r round(-b[3], 3)` | $-(\beta_2 + 6\beta_3)$ = `r round(-(b[3] + 6 * b[4]), 3)` | $-\beta_3$ = `r round(-b[4], 3)` |

:::

::: {.keybox}
Boys grow ≈ **`r round(b[2], 2)` mm/year**, girls ≈ **`r round(b[2] + b[4], 2)`**. The gap (boy − girl) grows from **`r round(-b[3], 1)`** to **`r round(-(b[3] + 6 * b[4]), 1)` mm**.
:::




---

## 7. How much do children differ? `VarCorr(o1)`

::: {.columns}

::: {.column width="45%"}

```{r}
#| label: q7-vc
VarCorr(o1)
icc(o1)
```

```{r}
#| label: q7-objects
#| include: false
vc <- as.data.frame(VarCorr(o1))
s_b <- vc$sdcor[1]; s_e <- vc$sdcor[2]
```

:::

::: {.column width="55%"}

::: {style="font-size: 0.85em"}

::: {.incremental}
- **SD of intercepts** ≈ **`r round(s_b, 2)` mm**: two children of the same sex differ, at 8, by about ± `r round(2 * s_b, 1)` mm (95%) around their sex mean.
- **Residual SD** ≈ `r round(s_e, 2)` mm: measurement noise + deviations from each child's line. Even if we knew each child's line, its measurements would still miss it by about **± 1.4 mm**.
- **ICC** = $\frac{`r round(s_b, 2)`^2}{`r round(s_b, 2)`^2 + `r round(s_e, 2)`^2}$ ≈ **`r round(s_b^2 / (s_b^2 + s_e^2), 2)`**: ≈ `r round(100 * s_b^2 / (s_b^2 + s_e^2))`% of the variance (beyond sex and age) is **between children**.
:::

::: {.fragment .note}
With a random intercept only, the ICC is also the **correlation between any two visits** of the same child (compound symmetry).
:::

:::

:::

:::

::: {.fragment .keybox}
**Consequences.** Two visits of the same child correlate ≈ 0.63: 108 measurements are worth much less than 108 independent points (`lm()` would give too-small SEs). Comparisons **between children** (boys vs girls at 8) are less precise than comparisons **within children** (growth rates).
:::


# {.divider background-color="#f7f6f3"}

<p class="eyebrow">Part D · Answer with emmeans</p>
<p class="bignum">D</p>
<h2>Questions 8–11</h2>
<p class="lead muted">Same numbers as by hand, now with SEs, CIs and p-values.</p>

---

## 8. Boys vs girls at 8 and at 14

::: {style="font-size: 0.65em"}

```{r}
#| label: q8-emm
emm <- emmeans(o1, ~ Sex | age_c, at = list(age_c = c(0, 6)))
emm
pairs(emm)
```

:::

```{r}
#| label: q8-objects
#| include: false
pr <- as_tibble(pairs(emm))
```

::: {style="font-size: 0.8em"}

::: {.keybox}
At 8: gap **`r round(pr$estimate[1], 2)` mm**, p = `r round(pr$p.value[1], 2)`. At 14: **`r round(pr$estimate[2], 2)` mm**, p `r format.pval(pr$p.value[2], digits = 1, eps = 0.001)`. Boys and girls are not distinguishable at 8, but clearly different at 14.
:::

:::

::: {.note}
p = `r round(pr$p.value[1], 2)` at 8 does **not** mean "same distance": look at the CI with `confint(pairs(emm))`. With 27 children, a 1–2 mm gap is hard to detect.
:::

---

## 9. Growth by sex: `emtrends`

::: {.columns}

::: {.column width="50%"}

::: {style="font-size: 0.65em"}

```{r}
#| label: q9-o1
tr1 <- emtrends(o1, ~ Sex, var = "age_c")
tr1
pairs(tr1)
```

```{r}
#| label: q9-objects
#| include: false
t1 <- as_tibble(tr1); p1 <- as_tibble(pairs(tr1))
```

:::

:::

::: {.column width="50%"}

::: {.incremental}
- **Boys** grow **`r round(t1$age_c.trend[1], 2)` mm/year** (95% CI `r round(t1$lower.CL[1], 2)`–`r round(t1$upper.CL[1], 2)`).
- **Girls** grow **`r round(t1$age_c.trend[2], 2)` mm/year** (95% CI `r round(t1$lower.CL[2], 2)`–`r round(t1$upper.CL[2], 2)`).
- Boys grow **`r round(p1$estimate, 2)` mm/year faster** (p = `r round(p1$p.value, 3)`).
:::

::: {.fragment .keybox}
Yes, boys grow faster: over the 6 years, ≈ `r round(6 * p1$estimate, 1)` mm more. Same numbers as by hand (question 6), now with SEs and a p-value.
:::

:::

:::

---


## 10. Difference of differences

::: {style="font-size: 0.65em"}

```{r}
#| label: q10-did
emm_8_14 <- emmeans(o1, ~ Sex * age_c, at = list(age_c = c(0, 6)))
did <- contrast(emm_8_14, interaction = c(Sex = "pairwise", age_c = "revpairwise"))
did
```

:::

```{r}
#| label: q10-objects
#| include: false
d <- as_tibble(did)
```

::: {.columns}

::: {.column width="50%"}

::: {.keybox}
Boys gain **`r round(d$estimate, 2)` mm more** than girls from 8 to 14 (p = `r round(d$p.value, 3)`).
:::

:::

::: {.column width="50%"}

::: {style="font-size: 0.8em"}

::: {.incremental}
- = gap at 14 − gap at 8 = `r round(pr$estimate[2], 2)` − `r round(pr$estimate[1], 2)` (question 8).
- = 6 years × `r round(p1$estimate, 3)` mm/year (question 9).
- = −6 × `age_c:SexFemale`: **same t and p** as that coefficient.
:::

:::

:::

:::

::: {.fragment .note}
With a straight line, "do they grow differently?", "does the gap change?" and "is there an interaction?" are **the same question**.
:::

---

## 11. Population curves with `ggpredict()`

::: {style="font-size: 0.55em"}

```{r}
#| label: q11-gg
#| fig-height: 4
pred <- ggpredict(o1, terms = c("age_c [0:6 by=0.5]", "Sex")) |>
  as_tibble() |>
  mutate(age = x + 8, Sex = group)

ggplot(pred, aes(age, predicted, color = Sex, fill = Sex)) +
  geom_line(data = ortho, aes(y = distance, group = Subject), alpha = .25, linewidth = .5) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = conf.low, ymax = conf.high), alpha = .2, color = NA) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 1.6) +
  scale_color_manual(values = pal_sex) + scale_fill_manual(values = pal_sex) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = c(8, 10, 12, 14)) +
  labs(x = "age (years)", y = "distance (mm)")
```

:::

::: {.note}
Thick lines: $X\hat\beta$, the **typical** boy and girl (marginal). Bands: 95% CI of the **mean**, not the range of children (the thin lines spread much wider). The bands separate as age increases: the result of question 8, seen as a picture.
:::

---

## 11b. The gap, age by age

::: {style="font-size: 0.6em"}

```{r}
#| label: q11-gap
#| fig-height: 3.6
gap <- emmeans(o1, ~ Sex | age_c, at = list(age_c = seq(0, 6, by = 0.5))) |>
  pairs() |>
  confint() |>
  as_tibble() |>
  mutate(age = age_c + 8)

ggplot(gap, aes(age, estimate)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", color = muted) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = lower.CL, ymax = upper.CL), fill = fact, alpha = .2) +
  geom_line(color = fact, linewidth = 1.3) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = c(8, 10, 12, 14)) +
  labs(x = "age (years)", y = "boy − girl distance (mm), 95% CI")
```

:::

::: {.keybox}
The **effect of sex** as a function of age: ≈ `r round(gap$estimate[1], 1)` mm at 8 (band crosses 0), ≈ `r round(gap$estimate[nrow(gap)], 1)` mm at 14. The band leaves 0 at about age **`r gap$age[which(gap$lower.CL > 0)[1]]`**. The slope of this line is `age_c:Sex`.
:::

::: {.note}
Pointwise 95% CIs: good for describing **from when** boys and girls differ, not a formal test at every age.
:::

---

## 11c. Growth rates by sex

::: {.columns}

::: {.column width="50%"}

::: {style="font-size: 0.6em"}

```{r}
#| label: q11-rates
#| fig-height: 3.8
#| fig-width: 6
as_tibble(tr1) |>
  ggplot(aes(age_c.trend, Sex, color = Sex)) +
  geom_pointrange(aes(xmin = lower.CL, xmax = upper.CL),
                  size = .8, linewidth = 1.2) +
  scale_color_manual(values = pal_sex, guide = "none") +
  labs(x = "growth rate (mm/year), 95% CI", y = NULL)
```

:::

:::

::: {.column width="50%"}

::: {style="font-size: 0.6em"}

```{r}
#| label: q11-rates-diff
#| fig-height: 3.8
#| fig-width: 6
confint(pairs(tr1)) |>
  as_tibble() |>
  ggplot(aes(estimate, contrast)) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", color = muted) +
  geom_pointrange(aes(xmin = lower.CL, xmax = upper.CL),
                  color = counter, size = .8, linewidth = 1.2) +
  labs(x = "difference in growth rate (mm/year), 95% CI", y = NULL)
```

:::

:::

:::

::: {.keybox}
Left: each sex's rate. Right: the **effect** (boys − girls), its CI does not cross 0 → boys grow faster. The left CIs overlap a bit, yet the difference is clear: compare **differences**, not overlapping intervals.
:::

---

## 11d. Each child vs its sex

::: {style="font-size: 0.6em"}

```{r}
#| label: q11-cond
#| fig-height: 3.8
ortho |>
  mutate(child_line = predict(o1),                 # Xβ + Zb_i (conditional)
         sex_line   = predict(o1, re.form = NA)) |> # Xβ       (marginal)
  ggplot(aes(age, color = Sex)) +
  geom_point(aes(y = distance), alpha = .3, size = 1.2) +
  geom_line(aes(y = child_line, group = Subject), alpha = .5) +
  geom_line(aes(y = sex_line), color = ink, linewidth = 1.6) +
  facet_wrap(~ Sex) +
  scale_color_manual(values = pal_sex, guide = "none") +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = c(8, 10, 12, 14)) +
  labs(x = "age (years)", y = "distance (mm)")
```

:::

::: {.keybox}
Thin lines: each child's fitted line, $X\hat\beta + Z\hat b_i$. Thick line: the sex's line, $X\hat\beta$. With `o1` children's lines are **parallel** to their sex's line (own level, common rate): exactly what the random intercept assumes.
:::

---

## 11e. Effects plot · each sex across ages

::: {style="font-size: 0.5em"}

```{r}
#| label: eff-sex-age
#| fig-height: 3
emm_grid <- emmeans(o1, ~ Sex | age_c, at = list(age_c = c(0, 2, 4, 6))) |>
  as_tibble() |>
  mutate(age = age_c + 8)

ggplot(emm_grid, aes(age, emmean, color = Sex, group = Sex)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 1, position = position_dodge(.3)) +
  geom_pointrange(aes(ymin = lower.CL, ymax = upper.CL), position = position_dodge(.3), size = .5) +
  scale_color_manual(values = pal_sex) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = c(8, 10, 12, 14)) +
  labs(x = "age (years)", y = "estimated mean distance (mm) ± 95% CI")
```

:::

::: {style="font-size: 0.8em"}

::: {.keybox}
One line per sex: **how each sex grows with age**. The slope of each line is its growth rate (`emtrends`); lines that **diverge** = Sex × age interaction.
:::

:::

---

## 11f. Effects plot · each age across sexes

::: {style="font-size: 0.5em"}

```{r}
#| label: eff-age-sex
#| fig-height: 3.4
ggplot(emm_grid, aes(Sex, emmean, color = factor(age), group = factor(age))) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 1) +
  geom_pointrange(aes(ymin = lower.CL, ymax = upper.CL), size = .5) +
  scale_color_viridis_d("age", end = .9) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "estimated mean distance (mm) ± 95% CI")
```

:::

::: {style="font-size: 0.7em"}

::: {.keybox}
Same estimates, axes swapped: one line per age, **how boys and girls compare at that age**. The slope of each line is the boy − girl gap: almost flat at 8, steeper at 14 → the sex effect **grows with age**. If there were no interaction, the lines would be **parallel** in both plots.
:::

:::

---

## Take-home

::: {style="font-size: 0.9em"}

::: {.incremental}
1. **Plot first**: different starts, parallel lines
2. **Random intercept** is enough (`o1`): a straight line is enough too.
3. Boys and girls start similar at 8 (gap ≈ 1.4 mm, n.s.) but **diverge**: ≈ 3.2 mm at 14.
4. Boys grow **≈ 0.3 mm/year faster**: the slope difference, the change in the gap and the interaction coefficient are the same number.
5. The covariance choice **does not change β̂** here, but it **changes SEs, df and p**.
:::

:::
